title: Module 1: Hello C
story_text:
# 🦕 The Dinosaur

C was created in 1972 by Dennis Ritchie. It runs the world (literally, kernels are written in C).

Use `printf` to talk.

title: Module 2: Format Specifiers
story_text:
# 🎭 Placeholders

`printf` needs to know the type.

- `%d`: Integer
- `%f`: Float
- `%c`: Char
- `%s`: String
hints: %f is for floats. Use %d for decimals (integers).

title: Module 3: Scanf (Input)
story_text:
# 📥 Scanf

`scanf("%d", &variable);`

Don't forget the `&` (address of) operator!
hints: scanf needs the ADDRESS of the variable.

title: Module 4: Pointers Basics
story_text:
# 👉 Pointing

`int *ptr` holds an address.
`*ptr` accesses the value.
quiz_data: [{"question": "Size of pointer on 64-bit?", "options": ["4 bytes", "8 bytes", "Depends", "2 bytes"], "answer": 1}]

title: Module 5: Strings (Char Arrays)
story_text:
# 🧵 String Theory

C has no `string` type. It has arrays of `char` ending with `\0` (null terminator).

`char name[] = "Bob";`
hints: "Hello" is 5 chars, but C strings need a \0 at the end.

title: Module 6: String Compare
story_text:
# ⚖️ Equality

You cannot use `==` on strings! It compares addresses.

Use `strcmp(a, b)` from `<string.h>`.
hints: If strcmp returns 0, they are equal.

title: Module 7: Malloc (Dynamic Memory)
story_text:
# 🏗️ Building Blocks

`malloc(size)` requests memory. Returns `void*`.

Always `free()` what you malloc!

title: Module 8: Structs
story_text:
# 📦 Packages

Structs hold related data.

`struct Point { int x; int y; };`

title: Module 9: Macros
story_text:
# 🔄 Text Replacement

`#define PI 3.14`

Macros are replaced BEFORE compilation.
hints: Don't put semicolons in #define values unless you really mean to.

title: Module 10: File I/O
story_text:
# 📂 Persistence

`FILE *f = fopen("file.txt", "w");`

Modes: "r" (read), "w" (write), "a" (append).

title: Module 11: Switch Fallthrough
story_text:
# 🕳️ Trapdoor

Cases fall through without `break`.

title: Module 12: Void Pointers
story_text:
# 🎭 The Actor

`void*` can point to anything. But you must cast it back to use it.

title: Module 13: Buffer Overflow
story_text:
# 💥 Boom

Writing past the end of an array corrupts memory.

title: Module 14: Enum
story_text:
# 🏷️ Labels

`enum State { IDLE, RUN, JUMP };`

title: Module 15: Typedef
story_text:
# 🎭 Nicknames

`typedef unsigned int uint;`

title: Module 16: Bitwise Ops
Module 17: Pre-increment vs Post-increment
story_text:
# ➕ The Difference

`++i`: Increment, then use.
`i++`: Use, then increment.
quiz_data: [{"question": "int i=0; int a=i++; What is a?", "options": ["0", "1", "2", "Error"], "answer": 0}]
hints: Use i++ to use the old value first.

title: Module 18: Recursion (Factorial)
Module 19: Command Line Args
story_text:
# 💻 CLI

`main(int argc, char *argv[])`

`argv[0]` is the program name.

title: Module 20: 2D Arrays
story_text:
# 🔳 Matrix

`int grid[3][3];`

Row first, then Column.
quiz_data: [{"question": "grid[y][x] usually means?", "options": ["Row y, Col x", "Col y, Row x", "Depths", "Time"], "answer": 0}]
